title: A finitely presented algebra has a model over one subfield
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ be a nonempty directed family of subfields of $k$ whose union is $k$, and let $E$ be a finitely presented commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Then for some $i\in I$ there is a commutative $K_i$-algebra $B$ and a $k$-algebra isomorphism $k\otimes_{K_i}B\cong E$. If $k:\mathrm{Type}\ u$ and $E:\mathrm{Type}\ w$, the carrier of $B$ can be chosen in $\mathrm{Type}(\max(u,w))$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields), proof, first three sentences: descend the finitely many polynomial relations and coefficients. The same construction applies to every finitely presented algebra.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation E ≅ k[X₁,...,Xₙ]/J with J finitely generated, using Algebra.FinitePresentation.iff. Choose a finite set s of ideal generators.

The union of the finite sets of nonzero coefficients of the polynomials in s is finite. Induction on this set, using hUnion, hdir and Nonempty I in the empty case, gives i with every coefficient in K i. MvPolynomial.mem_range_map_iff_coeffs_subset then lifts every relation to a polynomial over K i. Let J₀ be the ideal generated by these lifts and Q the quotient polynomial algebra over K i.

Polynomial scalar extension MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv identifies k ⊗[K i] (K i)[X₁,...,Xₙ] with k[X₁,...,Xₙ]. Tensoring the quotient uses Algebra.TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv, the quotient-base-change identity in its direct tensor formulation. Under the polynomial equivalence the extended ideal maps to J: Ideal.map_map and Ideal.map_span reduce this to the fact that each lifted relation maps to its original generator. Ideal.quotientEquivAlg thus gives k ⊗[K i] Q ≅ E.

Take B = ULift Q in Type (max u w). Tensor congruence with ULift.algEquiv transports the preceding equivalence and gives the claimed model in the required universe. This also covers zero algebras and presentations with no relations or no variables.
